sequenceDiagram
    accTitle: A complete feature delivery loop
    accDescr: An authorized TODO drives code and targeted evidence, followed by documentation and an honest status update.
    autonumber
    participant Developer
    participant Task as TODO contract
    participant Code
    participant Tests
    participant Docs
    Developer->>Task: Select scoped change and prerequisites
    Developer->>Code: Read callers and state ownership
    Developer->>Tests: Add targeted synthetic regression
    Developer->>Code: Implement complete slice
    Code->>Tests: Run relevant existing layers
    Tests-->>Developer: Actual outcomes and gaps
    Developer->>Docs: Update chapters, visuals and journal
    Developer->>Task: Record evidence and honest status

A useful test is tied to an invariant. "The app launches" would not have caught a late final poisoning the next session's IDs. A source-partial test that proves one track's final leaves the other pending text intact is much stronger for that specific requirement (tests\PhantomFudge.Core.Tests\SourceTranscriptTests.cs:1-80).

Working on a shared Windows desktop

An agent or test must not kill a running user's app to overwrite a locked executable. Build to an isolated output directory or create a new candidate. The native lifecycle script refuses to touch a preexisting PhantomFudge process and tracks only the processes it starts (scripts\Test-NativeLifecycle.ps1:16-22, :69-113).

Avoid parallel .NET commands that write the same project obj tree. Parallel research or independent Python checks are fine; two builds of the same Core project can race on generated cache files even when they use different final output directories. Compile once, then use --no-build where appropriate for follow-up checks.

The documentation fixture must never use real notes or chat content. It has its own command line path and validates a synthetic/no-recording result before copying images (src\PhantomFudge.App\App.xaml.cs:47-59, scripts\Export-HandbookScreenshots.ps1:1-95). A screenshot request is not authorization to capture a meeting or disable display affinity.

Failure tests worth keeping

The native harness covers authentication, framing, cancellation, bounded queues and delayed shutdown. Its entry point reports named groups and returns failure on a failing group (tests\PhantomFudge.Audio.Tests\Program.cs:18-71). Tests must also cover the interaction between layers: a fake device can fail after another input has started, or a final can arrive while UI Stop is still awaiting cleanup.

Python tests use injected recognizers for deterministic failure cases, while separate real-model fixtures prove that the production decoder can recognize generated speech. A fake recognizer is appropriate for protocol determinism, not evidence of speech accuracy. Conversely, one recognized synthetic sentence does not prove every cancellation path.

Interpreting results

Record source identity, environment, exact command, pass/failure, sample size and limitations. The implementation-status document is a bounded receipt, not a badge that everything is safe (docs\IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md:1-292).

For capture, an in-process RenderTargetBitmap image proves UI appearance. A cropped GDI fixture proves only the sampled local path. Neither proves what a remote participant sees. Run an intentionally unprotected positive control only outside a live presentation; it is supposed to be capturable.

Contributor exercises

  1. Locate the normal audio harness dispatch and explain why it does not open hardware.
  2. Identify which tests should change when a source label is added.
  3. Explain why a successful model fixture cannot replace a malformed-frame test.
  4. Write the expected sequence for Start, immediate Stop, then another Start.
  5. Choose the smallest checks for a theme-only change versus a protocol change.

Distribution and troubleshooting

TL;DR: Use Installation for the Windows11 x64 installer. It bundles runtime/models and adds guarded update/uninstall; the older source/setup ZIP is a different workflow. Consult the versioned release for available downloads and exact identities. Neither distribution promises that every machine or recorder is supported.

Installer versus development bundle

The new recipe publishes the app and native launcher self-contained, assembles an offline speech runtime/model payload and emits versioned Setup, optional Portable ZIP and checksums. The target is v0.2.0-preview.1 / Windows version 0.2.0.1, unsigned; release downloads are public. End users do not need PowerShell7, a system Python or the .NET SDK. Builds require actual generated-PCM inference and natural process exit, separately from import and dependency-metadata checks. (scripts/Build-Installer.ps1:30-44,76-114) (tools/Installer/release.json:1-8)

The Inno recipe is per-user, uses a stable AppId, rejects downgrades and unrecognized nonempty destinations, and gates update/uninstall on maintenance. Repair/update uses a fresh self-contained helper directory extracted from Setup rather than a potentially corrupted old launcher. Lifecycle3 passed the current candidate's isolated repair/lifecycle fixture. Uninstall invokes the installed launcher. WindowsVersion under HKCU\Software\PhantomFudge\Installer\<AppId> is the fallback for a damaged version file. It does not force-close an app. Save/export, stop capture and close with X first. External user settings, diagnostics and saved files are retained; do not save personal content inside managed program directories. The canonical guide explains the directory and retention policy. (tools/Installer/PhantomFudge.iss:10-40,47-65,107-161) (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/Program.cs:50-58,94-100) (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/MaintenanceOperation.cs:48-118)

The repository and its published prerelease downloads are now public. The owner authorized this prerelease work without making it a qualified release or selecting a project license. Unsigned-policy blocks must be respected, not bypassed. Exact hashes, lifecycle tests and publication state belong in implementation status, not inferred from this build recipe.

Setup never launches the app. Finish and close it, then open Phantom Fudge from Start. Setup and launcher status/error windows are ordinary visible UI, not capture-excluded; install and launch before sharing. (tools/Installer/PhantomFudge.iss:14-76) (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/LauncherWindow.cs:18-57)

If an ordinary or notes-only launch detects the installer gate, it returns70 with generic “operation busy” status, without opening a launcher window or starting a child. Let Setup finish and retry rather than deleting ownership files. The gate is checked before existing-instance reveal and again after acquiring the startup mutex; maintenance and layout validation bypass it. (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/Program.cs:25-78,240-244) (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/LauncherContract.cs:152-165) (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/LauncherStatus.cs:15,34)

App startup is not proven by surviving a short delay. The launcher retains its operation mutex until the main app mutex appears or the exact child exits. Status76 after30seconds is pending, not success; Close hides progress without releasing that guard, even if the dispatcher shuts down early. Uncertain liveness stays protected rather than authorizing replacement or process killing. (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/ChildProcesses.cs:12-42) (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/Program.cs:108-118,186-227)

Inventory and repair evidence are different checks

The final runtime is not a copy of the developer's venv: it uses pinned embedded CPython3.13.14, faster-whisper 1.2.1+phantomfudge1 for PCM-only input and CTranslate2 4.6.0+phantomfudge2 with oneDNN3.1.1/Microsoft compiler OpenMP (vcomp140). It excludes CUDA/cuDNN/proprietary Intel OpenMP and PyAV/FFmpeg. Variants/notices are listed in third-party notices. The parent confirms85 focused runtime tests; the final offline rebuild passes real generated-PCM hybrid inference, production VAD, forced Whisper encoder/decoder execution and natural exit, repeated after Unicode relocation. Vosk's unmodified package uses a first-party startup adapter for non-ASCII Windows model paths. The older Ruy stages failed at process exit and remain rejected; metadata closure alone describes only the modified installed graph and cannot establish execution. No actual capture, service, provider request or clean-VM test was performed by this runtime qualification. Final redistribution/provenance review remains separate from the passing lifecycle fixture, and existing development speech measurements must not be inherited by this different binary set. See dated runtime evidence for the exact payload identity. (tools/Installer/runtime-lock.json:1-11) (tools/Installer/bundle_runtime.py:246-282,332-376,412-462,538-609) (services/transcription/recognizer.py:44-63) (services/transcription/tests/test_packaged_pcm_runtime.py:35-97,126-138)

Fresh-machine confidence needs more than a restricted PATH. The frozen builder now checks PE normal/delay imports and exported forwarder DLL names against bundled files or a reviewed Windows11 inbox list, then observes actual DLL paths in its import and synthetic-PCM probes. The parent reports 92 speech PE files and five bundled CRT paths passing, plus a separate static pass over 861 app/launcher PE files. The final DLL-qualified runtime rebuild has passed this stronger gate and recorded new provenance; functional DLLs are reported unchanged from candidate2. Neither static closure nor these selected loaded-module observations are a clean-VM or universal dynamic-loading test. (tools/Installer/bundle_runtime.py:677-694) (tools/Installer/runtime_audit.py:126-166,169-234) (services/transcription/tests/test_packaged_pcm_runtime.py:14,88-97)

The launcher consumes compact install-manifest.json metadata with a16KiB size bound, while payload-files.json lists full payload paths, lengths and SHA-256 values. Separating them prevents the large runtime inventory from invalidating ordinary startup. The inventory includes the compact manifest but excludes its own self-hash. Build-Installer enumerates hidden files/directories and rejects reparse points and private payload paths before writing the inventory. (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/LauncherContract.cs:38-52,94-105) (scripts/Build-Installer.ps1:56-98)

Test-Installer.ps1 defines an isolated fixture with a random AppId and a separate installation path; shortcut creation is omitted and Setup has no launch action. It compares the inventory's filenames with the payload exactly, then checks installed lengths/hashes. Repair, damaged-launcher/version record recovery, downgrade rejection, uninstall and a retained synthetic external file are distinct assertions. The inspected lifecycle3 receipt passes 11 checks for 3,682 inventoried files from the parent's current-runtime candidate2 build. The earlier lifecycle2 result is historical. (scripts/Test-Installer.ps1:15-18,31-84) (tools/Installer/PhantomFudge.iss:62-76)

The “upgrade” case writes an older numeric version record into the current fixture. It does not install a genuine older binary or qualify a clean Windows VM, migration across actual releases, Start-menu behavior or the supported hardware matrix. Lifecycle3's PASS retains those limits. (scripts/Test-Installer.ps1:69-74,96-104)

The frozen launcher's separate --validate-install mode checks the owned marker, bounded compact manifest and expected file/model-directory layout without invoking the app, Python or inference. Historical pre-gate exact-EXE checks returned0for a synthetic valid layout and65for oversized/corrupt metadata. Placeholder layout validation is not a model-hash, native ABI, executable-launch or full installer-repair test. See current evidence. (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/Program.cs:25-43) (src/PhantomFudge.Launcher/LauncherContract.cs:87-105) (tests/PhantomFudge.Core.Tests/InstalledMaintenanceTests.cs:210-239)

Legacy overview: what gets shipped

Publish-Preview.ps1 builds a self-contained win-x64 application into a timestamped directory, copies a selected documentation/script/service allowlist, and creates a ZIP plus SHA256 output (scripts\Publish-Preview.ps1:1-52). The exact list matters: copying the repository wholesale would also risk models, token files, captures, temporary data and unrelated development tooling.

In this legacy ZIP, the native runtime and Python runtime are different dependencies. Self-contained .NET publishing includes the .NET runtime needed by the executable. It does not install Python, create the service's venv or embed either ASR model. Those operations are owned by explicit initialization (scripts\Initialize-Transcription.ps1:119-165).

Legacy candidate-to-qualified-release flow

Editable Mermaid source
---
config: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#2d333b","primaryBorderColor":"#6d5dfc","primaryTextColor":"#e6edf3","lineColor":"#8b949e","clusterBkg":"#161b22","clusterBorder":"#30363d"}}
---
flowchart TB
    accTitle: A local candidate is not a release
    accDescr: Source and allowlisted inputs produce a hashed archive; extracted-copy operation and qualification are separate subsequent activities.
    Source["Source and lock files"] --> Publish["Self-contained native publish"]
    Allowlist["Selected docs and Python source"] --> Bundle["Candidate directory"]
    Publish --> Bundle
    Bundle --> Archive["Timestamped ZIP and hash"]
    Archive --> Fresh["Fresh extracted-copy setup"]
    Fresh --> Native["Native service and UI checks"]
    Native --> Qualify["Hardware and recipient qualification"]
    Qualify --> Approval["Owner-authorized release"]

The final arrows describe qualification, not a prerequisite for honestly labelled experimental prerelease access. They are deliberately not automatic. A passing local smoke test is not signing, distribution authorization, enterprise-policy acceptance or four-product capture qualification. The implementation-status document identifies the actual local candidate and its remaining boundaries (docs\IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md:1-322).

Source checkout versus legacy extracted bundle

The launcher detects whether PhantomFudge.exe sits at the root of its working package. If it does, it uses that executable without building. Otherwise it targets the source-build path. An already-running source instance is revealed rather than rebuilt underneath the user (scripts\Run-PhantomFudge.ps1:8-36).

Situation Correct action Avoid
First source setup Run explicit initialization with model-download permission Expecting the app to fetch weights during a meeting
First extracted bundle Keep the full folder, then run its setup/launcher Copying only the EXE away from dependent files
Existing app running Save/close when an update requires replacement, or reveal it Killing an unknown process to release a file lock
Notes-only use Use the explicit NotesOnly launcher option Pretending a missing ASR service is healthy
Speech service idle Use its managed Stop command Broad process-name termination
Service active Stop transcription in the UI first Discarding queued audio by terminating the backend

Legacy setup is intentionally explicit

The initializer checks a pinned archive size/hash and verifies the extracted model files. An existing damaged model is not silently overwritten. Token creation uses random bytes, does not rotate an existing valid token automatically, and restricts the Windows DACL (scripts\Initialize-Transcription.ps1:26-76, :69-109).

The recorded archive hash is an observed integrity value from a known public download, not a publisher-signed guarantee. That distinction is explained in the service guide (services\transcription\README.md:140-235).

Vosk and Whisper models can be reused from verified local caches. The native default is hybrid-whisper/small.en/int8/four threads/technical vocabulary; explicit legacy Vosk or base.en are configuration choices, not automatic fallbacks. The new allowlisted runtime includes accurate/configuration/diagnostics/provisioning modules and both model/vocabulary manifests. (services/transcription/configuration.py:11-35,61-70.) Dependency repair is controlled by the requirements hash/import check and stays in the service's venv. Setup does not mean recording; launching the service still leaves audio idle until the user presses Start.

Service ownership is more than a port

A listening port may belong to another workspace or process. The manager authenticates /v1/runtime, checks the service identifier/management version and matches the saved instance ID before reuse or shutdown (services\transcription\manage.py:114-159). A stale owned idle service can be restarted for a changed speech protocol, engine/model/source fingerprint, but active transcription is refused and the selected model is verified before replacement.

---
flowchart TB
    accTitle: Diagnose readiness through ownership
    accDescr: A listening port requires authenticated identity before reuse; absence requires explicit setup and an owned startup.
    Start["Start requested"] --> Port{"Port listening?"}
    Port -- no --> Setup["Check explicit model and token"]
    Setup --> Spawn["Spawn owned native service"]
    Spawn --> Ready["Wait for authenticated readiness"]
    Port -- yes --> Identity["Authenticate and match instance"]
    Identity -->     Compatible{"Current protocol and runtime?"}
    Compatible -- yes --> Reuse["Reuse without restart"]
    Compatible -- no --> Active{"Transcription active?"}

    Active -- no --> Restart["Owned graceful restart"]

This design refuses ambiguity instead of adopting an arbitrary process. The manager's status output intentionally reports only readiness/activity/PID, not token or transcript content (services\transcription\manage.py:244-268).

Troubleshooting by symptom

The window is missing

First distinguish Hidden, minimized, failed initialization and a different running instance. Ctrl+Alt+Space and relaunch recovery are intended paths. The single-instance pipe accepts one fixed recovery command under current-user restrictions, not arbitrary scripts or filenames (src\PhantomFudge.App\Native\SingleInstance.cs:18-75).

If protection setup fails, the app withholds content and records a generic local notice rather than displaying an unprotected branded error window (src\PhantomFudge.App\LocalFailureNotice.cs:1-30). That notice is diagnostic data, not saved notes.

Start fails

Check the selected input mode, every requested device, local token, model and service version. In Both mode, a missing microphone must not silently become Computer-only. The native adapter validates selection and waits for protocol readiness before opening inputs (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\LoopbackTranscriber.cs:72-156).

Nothing is transcribed

A selected playback endpoint may not be the meeting application's actual output. A microphone may be muted or denied by Windows policy. A zero meter and an empty transcript are not enough to diagnose the same problem. Do not "fix" either by opening a different device automatically. Actual hardware diagnosis needs explicit user authorization and the named device configuration.

Stop seems slow

The application may be releasing native inputs, draining accepted audio or waiting for final recognition. IsRunning is not a complete shutdown contract. A hung native call cannot be safely treated as disposed merely because a UI timeout expired. The source retains ownership and blocks unsafe restart rather than using a success-shaped fallback.

Answers are slow or return no useful solution

Separate provider preparation, first text, complete answer/session close and UI assignment. Startup/reveal/reload prepares one empty Agency session without inference; cold preparation can take roughly 20–31 seconds. Wait for Ready, then Ask. Three prepared exact-text GPT-5.6 Sol Fast / low responses completed below five seconds; this does not guarantee future latency. Earlier fast wrong answers and slow cases remain in the quality record. (src/PhantomFudge.App/MainWindow.AnswerLifetime.cs:23-78.)

Default local diagnostics provide request/capture IDs, stages, counts and safe errors, not conversation bodies. Show-Diagnostics.ps1 excludes synthetic UI timings by default. Export-Diagnostics.ps1 strips Text unless explicitly requested and includes only four allowlisted metadata-only speech logs from that workspace; it does not upload anything (scripts/Export-Diagnostics.ps1:14-80; src/PhantomFudge.Core/Diagnostics/LocalDiagnostics.cs:20-24,40-69).

Docker is missing

Normal native operation does not require it. Docker recipes are optional final-stage packaging. Only an explicit Docker mode should require a Docker engine (scripts\Start-Transcription.ps1:1-35). Do not turn a portability task back into a mandatory infrastructure dependency.

Release discipline

Keep candidate names/hashes immutable. If source, runtime, rendering or protocol changes, create a new candidate and rerun the affected evidence. Signed versus unsigned status must be explicit; signing does not guarantee SmartScreen or organizational acceptance.

The handbook and journal are now part of that discipline. A release that changes what the user sees needs current screenshots; a protocol change needs a current sequence diagram and source references. Freshness tooling detects changed inputs, but semantic review remains the author's job.

  • scripts\Publish-Preview.ps1:1-52 — package recipe.
  • scripts\Initialize-Transcription.ps1:26-165 — model/token/runtime setup.
  • scripts\Run-PhantomFudge.ps1:8-57 — source/package launch selection.
  • services\transcription\manage.py:114-268 — instance ownership, reuse and stop.
  • src\PhantomFudge.App\Native\SingleInstance.cs:18-75 — window recovery channel.
  • src\PhantomFudge.App\LocalFailureNotice.cs:1-30 — non-content failure notice.

Source: docs/WEBSITE.md

Phantom Fudge Website and Tutorial Pipeline

The site directory is a standalone static landing page. It uses the canonical DeepSeaFoam palette, original ghost artwork, motion controls, sample-data GIFs, and a full chaptered tutorial. The native application and published installer are separate products; this website does not run transcription, sign into a provider, collect notes or change Windows capture behavior. The publication boundary is deliberately small: the assembler reads site/media.json, verifies the web MP4 already bundled under site/media, and copies only site, not the repository. Normal assembly needs no original production tutorial, release download, LFS or media secret. (tools/Site/build.mjs:28-52; tools/Site/test-site.mjs:98-130)

Final local source freeze: the bundled web video is86,168,722bytes with SHA256 28cd9c871b96e6db6cc4f14d740942c388a6abd235d8ba4e4031cf50ec75fc71. It retains2297.767seconds,1920x1080,30fps and68,933frames. All eight GIF sets and the final page/browser integration were reviewed locally; publication remains pending. (site/media.json:1-27)

Less visible text, not less visual design

The owner's clarification is less visible text only. Keep the DeepSeaFoam palette, original ghosts, glow, mist, orbits and decorative motion. The short hero and eight one-line demo captions replace repeated explanations; the transcript and About this demo use closed-by-default disclosures. A compact privacy/capture-limit note stays visible below the tutorial rather than being hidden with those details. Long feature/privacy sections are not duplicated on this page. (site/index.html:24-57,58-120,157-185; site/styles.css:1-6,55-65,131-145)

The browser fixture counts the default rendered body's visible words and caps that state at350. That is a regression guard for copy density, not a request to strip artwork, delete accessible labels, truncate the complete transcript or claim human design approval. (tools/Site/review-browser.mjs:36-49,82-84)

The previous served page measured616default-visible words; the frozen revision measures276, a 340-word reduction. The transcript and About text still exist behind their disclosures, and the DeepSeaFoam ghosts, glow, mist, orbits and eight demonstrations remain visible.

Watch and navigate

The video supports native controls plus Play/Pause, back/forward ten seconds, playback speed and optional extra captions. Captions are also embedded in the MP4. Five chapters and six transcript results appear per page, with explicit previous/next buttons instead of nested scrolling. Open the collapsed transcript panel to search. Search is literal and case-insensitive; selecting a result seeks without autoplay. Scope details also start collapsed.

The eight large GIF demonstrations use keyboard-accessible tabs rather than tiny previews. Pause motion freezes ghosts and replaces animated GIFs with stills. Reduced-motion visitors start with static artwork. No JavaScript means native video, static demo images and downloadable chapter/caption files; enhanced search and chapter buttons require JavaScript.

Demo ID Tutorial chapter ID Retained sample action

transcription transcription Explicit Start, then later Stop

Each assets/demo-<id> has GIF, JPEG and MP4 derivatives at1000x720. The page uses the GIF/still pair; its image link seeks the associated full-tutorial chapter without starting playback. Retained spans run at1x; labelled jumps to later actions/results are not response-latency evidence. The original selection/context/cover triplets remain protected, not silently re-encoded. (site/index.html:71-120; site/app.mjs:150-197; tools/Site/make-demo-media.py:26-159,430-477)

These are scripted, sample-data demonstrations using actual WPF frames and synthetic narration. The current-source Previous answer feature is not in v0.2.0-preview.1. Native installation, file-picker and provider steps in the tutorial are instructions, not recordings of those operations.

The player behavior is implemented in app.mjs and its pure timing/search helpers. The existing browser fixture exercises all chapter starts, search and caption controls; the Node tests check all 525 cue intervals. Those checks do not establish live meeting, provider or capture compatibility. The expanded fixtures require eight demo triplets and exercise their chapter jumps, Home/End and arrow-key wrapping without autoplay. A failed video request must show a visible error while search remains available. (tools/Site/review-browser.mjs:51-148,178-193; tools/Site/test-site.mjs:22-50,80-111)

Final local gates passed14Node test cases and nine muted-browser review groups. A second build/test from an isolated fresh public-only tree also passed without the private original tutorial.

Assembly boundary

The bundled full video must be a reviewed input, not a generated side effect of the website build. The source-tree walk rejects symlinks, non-file entries and any individual file at or above 100 MiB. Total source size must be below 1,000,000,000 bytes. The media filename must be a simple MP4 basename; its declared size and streamed SHA256 must match the bundled payload. All those checks precede deletion of the previous preview. Copying itself is not atomic and has no rollback guarantee. (tools/Site/build.mjs:8-44)

These checks are not a general sanitizer for arbitrary files placed under site. Keep every input public-safe and run the bounded text scan and asset-integration tests. The failure fixture checks missing media, wrong bytes, same-size corruption, path traversal and the size boundary, and confirms that rejected inputs leave the old output intact. (tools/Site/test-site.mjs:64-96,113-159)

Local preview

Node 22 or later is sufficient to assemble and serve the complete checked-out site. No package installation, separate video argument or access to the original tutorial workspace is needed.

node .\tools\Site\build.mjs
node .\tools\Site\serve.mjs 4173

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/phantom-fudge/. The preview server binds only to loopback and supports HTTP byte ranges for seeking. Assembly replaces only the generated artifacts/site directory. The server accepts a single start-based range, including an open end, returns 416 for invalid ranges, and handles HEAD without sending the body. It is a local review server, not the Pages deployment. (tools/Site/serve.mjs:10-45)

The retained final review instance is http://127.0.0.1:4187/phantom-fudge/; it was not restarted for documentation generation. Port4173 above remains the tool's default for a future independent run.

# Keep test/browser scratch in the repository when required by local policy.
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\.local\site-review-scratch | Out-Null
$env:TEMP = (Resolve-Path .\.local\site-review-scratch).Path
$env:TMP = $env:TEMP
node --test .\tools\Site\test-site.mjs
node .\tools\Site\review-browser.mjs http://127.0.0.1:4173/phantom-fudge/

The browser review uses the existing tools/Docs Puppeteer dependency and an isolated, muted Edge profile. Set EDGE_PATH if needed. Review screenshots and receipts stay in ignored .local/site-review. Both the browser profile and the assembly test fixture use Node's OS scratch-directory selection and are removed in finally; the commands above redirect that selection for the current shell. The browser fixture observes external requests and fails if any occur; it is not a network-blocking browser sandbox. (tools/Site/review-browser.mjs:9-35,194-202; tools/Site/test-site.mjs:113-159)

GitHub Pages deployment

The repository's Pages source must be GitHub Actions. .github/workflows/pages.yml builds on website-related pushes to main or manual dispatch. It tests and assembles the checked-out website, including the bundled web video, then uploads only artifacts/site. There is no dedicated tutorial-release prerequisite in the current workflow. The original159,267,662-byte production MP4 remains separate from the Git-sized web derivative. That preserved original, not the web copy, has SHA256 388ee914e1ffdc0ac3911d2a2e8dc6c8f33d8aad047f1aeff02fbe41138e1fde. (.github/workflows/pages.yml:3-37; tools/Site/build.mjs:28-52; tools/Site/prepare-web-video.py:21-28)

Pinned Actions and job-scoped permissions separate artifact construction from Pages deployment. No secrets, private source inventories, local paths, context stores or repository-wide archives belong in the Pages artifact. The workflow source gives the build job contents: read for checkout and pages: read so configure-pages can read the Pages configuration. It runs Node 22 tests and the hash-verifying assembler. Only the dependent deploy job receives pages: write and id-token: write, using the github-pages environment. cancel-in-progress: false keeps a newer run from cancelling the current deployment. (.github/workflows/pages.yml:12-50; tools/Site/build.mjs:28-52)

Publication status: pending. The owner chose local completion rather than an authentication change after the active CLI account proved read-only. The later self-contained revision removes the separate media-release prerequisite; it does not authorize a push or deployment. An authorized maintainer must publish the complete reviewed source tree and verify the workflow and live site separately. The decisions are recorded in workstream61. Neither a prepared workflow nor a local browser pass means the website URL is live.

Updating the tutorial

node .\tools\Site\import-tutorial.mjs <completed-tutorial-directory> imports allowlisted public chapter/caption data from the tutorial identified by site/media.json. It does not import private delivery inventories. The generated module projects chapter IDs/titles/times and cue times/text; the five named chapter/caption files are copied intact and must themselves be public-safe. The source manifest must match media.original.sha256, while chapter duration must agree with the web video within 50 ms. Import compares metadata, not the MP4 payload. The top-level file, sha256, bytes, duration and format fields identify the bundled web copy; the nested original record identifies its preserved production source. They are not interchangeable: the assembler hashes the top-level web payload, and the importer checks the nested original identity. Changing the video requires a new reviewed asset identity; do not silently overwrite a published video with different bytes. (site/media.json:1-27; tools/Site/build.mjs:31-39; tools/Site/import-tutorial.mjs:10-33)

Full-video preparation is a separate local operation. prepare-web-video.py recompresses the full uncropped video with H.264 and copies the original AAC stream; it supplies no cut, scale or retiming filter. Its validator compares duration, frame count, dimensions, frame rate, start and chapters, verifies AAC payload/timestamp and decoded-PCM hashes, checks faststart, and decodes all 68,933 video frames plus audio. The hard limit is below 100 MiB; the 90 MiB target is recorded separately. Lossy video recompression still requires inspection of decoded output, not just matching metadata. (tools/Site/prepare-web-video.py:44-56,89-139,172-218)

The audio gate permits only the original final AAC duration of 832 samples or its normalization to 800 samples. Nonfinal durations, payloads, PTS/DTS, decoded PCM and decoded frame timing must match, as must audio-track/container duration. That possible 32-sample metadata adjustment is not a claim of lost audio or a listening test. (tools/Site/prepare-web-video.py:173-208)

# Reproduce the selected final CRF after inspecting representative samples.
python .\tools\Site\prepare-web-video.py --samples --crf 30
python .\tools\Site\prepare-web-video.py --encode --validate --crf 30

These commands require the original completed tutorial and the existing Python media dependencies. They never overwrite that original. Validation writes local provenance and review frames with visual review explicitly pending; it does not itself update site/media.json or import captions. For this frozen revision, separate inspection covered17contact-sheet times and six native1080p frames after the complete decode. The measured web/original identities were then registered in public metadata and the import, assembly and browser gates passed. Pass the actual encoding CRF when validating separately: the receipt records that argument, not a detected encoder setting. (tools/Site/prepare-web-video.py:198-248; tools/Site/import-tutorial.mjs:13-33)

The public assets/media-manifest.json records source/media identity and demo limitations. assets/asset-provenance.json records the GIF excerpts and artwork sources. Theme credit lives in site/THEME-NOTICE.txt; no sibling showcase artwork or fonts are copied.

Source-atlas coverage

Website source is not excluded just because it lives at the repository root. The atlas requires reviewed, contiguous explanations for site/index.html, styles.css, app.mjs, player-core.mjs, media.json and 404.html, as well as every in-scope Site tool and the Pages workflow. Source: docs/handbook/17-privacy-and-assurance.md

Privacy and assurance

TL;DR: The application can control its own inputs, storage, windows and requests. It cannot turn those controls into a universal guarantee about another recorder, the operating system, an administrator, a camera or a person. Assurance requires both a mechanism and the right experiment for the claim.

Overview: separate the questions

"Private" can mean that notes are absent from a recipient's frames, audio stays local, a token is not logged, a file is encrypted, or a process is not listed. Those are different properties. The current product explicitly does not promise process invisibility or a security/DRM boundary (docs\PRODUCT.md:209-225).

The first useful threat-model step is therefore to state what is controlled. The app owns its HWND and can request display affinity. It owns the selected capture objects and can require explicit Start. It owns the local protocol and can authenticate it. It does not own a meeting application's cursor-inclusion setting, the Windows microphone indicator or a camera aimed at the display.

Trust boundaries

Editable Mermaid source
---
config: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#2d333b","primaryBorderColor":"#6d5dfc","primaryTextColor":"#e6edf3","lineColor":"#8b949e","clusterBkg":"#161b22","clusterBorder":"#30363d"}}
---
flowchart TB
    accTitle: Current and proposed data boundaries
    accDescr: Selected input remains between the desktop and authenticated local recognizer; local saves and proposed Azure egress require explicit actions.
    Owner["Explicit owner action"] --> App["Desktop process"]
    Devices["Selected Windows inputs"] --> App
    App --> Local["Authenticated local Python"]
    Local --> App
    App --> Files["Explicit local saves"]
    App --> Logs["Local metadata; text opt-in"]
    App -->|"explicit exact question"| Hosted["Configured Agency model service"]
    App --> Display["Windows compositor"]
    Display --> Recorder["External recorder"]
    Recorder --> Audience["Recipient"]
    App -. "future explicit text only" .-> Azure["PLANNED Azure request"]

The compositor/recorder boundary is deliberately outside the local socket boundary. Securing localhost traffic does not prove pixel exclusion; setting display affinity does not authenticate the local service.

Window and cursor controls

The visual Cover is not a process or screen-reader invisibility feature. It detaches the disabled workspace and refreshes the current window-peer children while retaining data and ongoing work. Fresh in-process traversal sees the cover, but an already-retained value provider still reads the synthetic question. The native protection path also requests DWMWA_DISALLOW_PEEK; setter acceptance is not shell-preview or recipient qualification. The complete feasibility matrix separates these implemented measures from cached clients, process/memory inspection, unsupported capture paths and physical observation.

WindowProtection.Configure checks the platform/composition path, updates owned-window styles, requests exclusion and records readback. It does not inject into a recorder or change a global system privacy setting (src\PhantomFudge.App\Native\WindowProtection.cs:19-48).

The cursor policy chooses the standard Arrow for the app, while the default Present mode avoids unnecessary activation. The owner still reported a recipient-side disappearing pointer, and that exact sharing configuration remains unqualified. Local shape/foreground observations are useful but not substitutes for recipient frames (docs\CURSOR-AND-THEMES.md:1-69, src\PhantomFudge.App\Native\CursorPolicy.cs:1-25).

Automatic protection failures should not reveal the application through a new unprotected message box. A generic, bounded local notice contains no note/transcript payload (src\PhantomFudge.App\LocalFailureNotice.cs:1-30). Explicit OS file/auth surfaces are still separate from the main protected window.

Audio authority and retention

The later microphone request changed product authority: Computer, Mic or Both may be selected, but no endpoint opens before Start. Source labels are not people. Computer can include other app audio and sidetone; Mic can include speaker echo. Headphones reduce one practical risk but do not create an acoustic-echo-cancellation guarantee (docs\DUAL-SOURCE-AUDIO.md:1-26).

Raw audio is handled as bounded in-memory frames. The test harness uses synthetic PCM and must not implicitly open real devices. This is a meaningful policy, but it is not a claim of secure memory erasure, immunity to dumps, or control over host swap/administrators.

Local service authentication

The server uses a bounded local token, constant-time comparison, a one-active-session admission rule and explicit frame limits. Management operations additionally match an instance identity; they are not arbitrary process-control APIs (services\transcription\server.py:71-215, services\transcription\manage.py:155-200).

A malicious process running as the same user or an administrator is not contained by calling the service "localhost." The token and current-user boundaries reduce accidental/cross-context access; they do not transform the workstation into a trusted enclave. The service itself does not open microphones or read chats; the C# client owns the selected device operations.

Storage boundaries

Notes are not automatically persisted. Transcripts remain memory-only unless explicitly exported or diagnostic Text mode is enabled. Default logs record metadata without conversation bodies. Explicit file saves are bounded UTF-8 operations with conflict checks and same-directory replacement (src\PhantomFudge.Core\NoteFileStore.cs:16-91). Ordinary file deletion does not establish secure erasure from SSDs, backups or snapshots. An unsaved warning prevents one kind of data loss, not every crash.

Do not log note hashes as a supposedly harmless substitute for text. A short predictable question can be dictionary-tested against a hash. Use random correlation IDs and counts where diagnostics need identity without content.

App logs rotate at 2 MiB with at most ten files and a 1024-record nonblocking queue; dropped/failed records are observable. Backend logs rotate separately at 1 MiB with three backups and never include transcript text. Their identities are independent: correlate UTC/source/stages without inventing a shared session ID. Text opt-in does not add notes, audio, tokens or provider stderr. Local export removes Text by default and never uploads (src/PhantomFudge.Core/Diagnostics/LocalDiagnostics.cs:20-24,40-110; scripts/Export-Diagnostics.ps1:14-80; diagnostics).

Evidence ladder

Editable Mermaid source

flowchart LR
    accTitle: The evidence ladder
    accDescr: Reading code, synthetic observations, hardware behavior and recipient capture support successively scoped claims; missing evidence stays open.
    Code["Read mechanism"] --> Local["Local synthetic behavior"]
    Local --> Hardware["Named hardware scenario"]
    Hardware --> Remote["Named recipient capture"]
    Remote --> Claim["Scoped support claim"]
    Missing["Missing evidence"] --> Open["Keep qualification open"]
    Local -. "not equivalent" .-> Claim

A screenshot in this book is an actual WPF visual-tree render with generated content. It proves that the controls can render, not that a recorder did or did not capture them. A GDI positive/negative fixture is a different experiment. A remote meeting capture is different again. The qualification matrix names these dimensions and failure cases (docs\QUALIFICATION.md:1-40).

The same separation applies to speech: fake decoder tests prove deterministic protocol handling; a real recognizer with generated audio proves integration; real-speaker/device/echo tests establish a different scope. No single green test count can replace the others.

The planned Azure boundary

The local question implementation does not cross that boundary. It copies only explicitly selected structured segments or typed text, and freezes the displayed draft on explicit Ask. Source references stay local, including original text that may differ after editing. A future provider must use ExactText as its question payload; serializing the complete snapshot would defeat that separation. Snapshot-only mode sends nothing. An explicitly configured Agency provider is connected and normally uses hosted inference, while the local-model option has a separate loopback endpoint. Neither is a direct Azure adapter. Startup/reveal/reload may prepare one empty Agency session without a prompt; only explicit Ask sends question data (src/PhantomFudge.App/MainWindow.AnswerLifetime.cs:23-78). (src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionDraft.cs:18-95; src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionSnapshot.cs:5-23; local guide.)

The future Ask design intentionally sends a chosen immutable question, not the whole transcript. Cloud audio is optional and separately configured. Model text is displayed as data, not executed as code or used to choose tools/URLs. The desktop is a public client and must not contain a distributed application secret (docs\AI-ANSWER-PRIVACY.md:1-108).

store:false is not universal zero retention, and a resource's nominal region does not necessarily pin all Global deployment processing to that region. Those statements belong in the product contract before cloud execution, not after an incident. At this edition, Azure Ask is design only; no direct Azure identity/profile or Azure latency result exists. Installed Agency has its own bounded measured results, not evidence that an Azure deployment or universal five-second SLO exists.

Explicit prior text is another disclosure, not a permission escalation

The local-source Previous answer toggle is off by default and sends nothing until Ask. Then it includes one displayed completed answer, not the previous question, full meeting or nested history. That text may contain sensitive quotations, so the user can inspect it and the exact submitted copy under Setup/details. Busy work/active clarification locks the toggle; Clear and provider changes reset it. Existing provider/OS/diagnostic retention limits still apply. (Context controller.)

The prompt labels prior text as background, not an instruction, task mode or tool grant. Nonblank strict Unicode and32768UTF-16 units bound the field; fresh sessions and existing tool denial remain. Synthetic input/transport checks are not a universal prompt-injection resistance or model-quality proof. This increment does not requalify recipient capture or alter published v0.2.0-preview.1 assets. (Prompt policy, request validation, workstream59.)

Review questions

  1. What evidence would establish that an actual Teams screen-share mode excludes the new answer pane?
  2. Which data could still be visible through an OS indicator or an explicit file dialog?
  3. Why is the source label Mic not proof that the owner spoke?
  4. Why does local authentication not defend against every same-user process?
  5. What must an Azure Ask implementation avoid logging even when diagnostics are enabled?

18. Extending the System

Why a small feature can require a wide review

An extension is safe when its responsibilities are narrow and its consequences are traced completely. Adding a source is not just another selector; it affects byte framing, queue budgets, timestamp validation, stop behavior, display provenance, tests, and privacy wording. Adding a theme is not just changing a background; selection, disabled controls, alpha composition, and capture qualification also matter. The architecture explicitly prefers small testable interfaces over a generic plugin framework. (docs\ARCHITECTURE.md:47-86, component responsibilities; src\PhantomFudge.Core\AudioSource.cs:3-30, source identity; src\PhantomFudge.App\ThemeBrushes.cs:9-32, semantic resources.)

This chapter teaches change analysis; it does not add runtime capabilities. TODO28 established structured questions and exact Freeze; the Agency provider now uses persistent ACP with controlled fresh sessions. “Ask never sends” applies only to SnapshotOnly. Source commit29 and direct Azure30/31 remain separate future work, not prerequisites for reviewed explicit Ask. (src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:265-305, QuestionAsk_Click; TODO\29_QUESTION_COMMIT_LATENCY.todo:13-22, protocol tasks; TODO\30_AZURE_ANSWER_CONNECTION.todo:13-22, prerequisites.)

Missing settings select SnapshotOnly, and the parent restored that mode after stopping the owned login. The owner requests existing installed Agency, with no new login or organization-data access; LocalModel remains separate. The earlier Copilot smoke failed at the customization/tool gate and consumed its allowance because a model call cannot be ruled out. The successful Agency probe had new, separate authorization, not a retry of that allowance. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerConfiguration.cs:13-29, Load; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerContracts.cs:33-39, modes.) See provider boundaries and workstream39.

The marker smoke remains connectivity history. The completed authorized ledger records 48 client question submissions, including failed/superseded trials; no further model calls are planned. Agency 2026.10.7.4 / Copilot 1.0.92 now defaults to the advertised and tested gpt-5.6-sol-fast / low. H's three prepared exact-text responses completed usefully in 4.066, 4.176 and 2.992 s; all three implementations compiled and passed 33/33 checks. Two inputs used intended wording and one the owner's actual ASR string. These are provider observations, not app/voice acceptance or a universal SLO. LocalModel has mocks only; credentials may expire. (tools\AgencyProbe\results\summary-final.json:2-64, scope/results; tools\AgencyProbe\results\latency-suite-20261009-h-exact-fast.json:2-56, exact-text trials; tools\AgencyProbe\results\latency-suite-20261009-h-quality.json:2-186, compiled checks.)

Keep the failed path visible. Haiku E's five fast original-variation responses were not exact owner-ASR evidence. Haiku F chose two wrong problems and appended one follow-up; mini G understood all six exact questions but failed ten full-range overflow checks. H's selected result does not erase either. Cold Haiku took 24.874 s; first transport-only Asks took 5.041 s on F and 6.470 s on G. Never turn a prepared-session success into a cold-start promise. (tools\AgencyProbe\results\latency-suite-20261009-f-exact.json:2-98, retained failures; tools\AgencyProbe\results\summary-final.json:58-73, cold/transport boundaries; tools\AgencyProbe\results\summary-final.json:141-180, E–H comparison.)

The key discipline is to write the invariant before the edit. “A selected source cannot borrow another source's queue allowance” is testable. “Support more audio” is not. Existing tests already express this distinction through canonical schemas, bounded per-source resources, independent timing, and explicit rejection of undeclared input. (services\transcription\tests\test_dual_protocol.py:57-92, StartSchemaTests; services\transcription\tests\test_dual_protocol.py:150-200, independent tracks; services\transcription\tests\test_dual_protocol.py:250-255, undeclared-source rejection.)

Architecture: trace both directions across the boundary

For audio changes, follow data downstream from selected device to rendered transcript, then follow failures upstream to cancellation and cleanup. The local capture GUID is now attached to events before dispatcher delivery; a stale callback must not acquire the identity of a later Start. The unchanged display/export buffer and new structured question store are separate consumers, not interchangeable representations. (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\LoopbackTranscriber.cs:86-136, StartCoreAsync; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:194-237, TryEnqueueAudio; services\transcription\server.py:394-498, Session.recognize; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.xaml.cs:796-824, ReceiveTranscript; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:134-153, UpdateQuestionTranscript.)

This map is intentionally not a claim that every box is a formal interface. For example, Python expects recognizer objects with accept and finish, returning Recognition; C# injects a capture-construction delegate for tests. Understanding the actual seam prevents introducing abstraction machinery that the code does not need. (services\transcription\recognizer.py:17-22, Recognition; services\transcription\server.py:394-498, recognizer calls; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\LoopbackTranscriber.cs:18-28, capture injection.)

Checklist 1: a new audio source

Start with product meaning. Define what the source captures, how the user chooses it, and what its label does not mean. Current Computer and Mic labels identify inputs, not speakers; no source addition should silently become diarization or automatic meeting discovery. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\AudioSource.cs:16-30, AudioSourceNames; tests\PhantomFudge.Core.Tests\SourceTranscriptTests.cs:81-87, LabelsDescribeInputNotSpeaker.)

Then inspect these concrete surfaces:

  1. Identity and selection: extend the enum and explicit selection model deliberately. AudioInputSelection currently has only two device fields; ValidateSelection constructs at most two inputs and rejects duplicate device IDs. A new enum value alone is insufficient. (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptEvent.cs:5-7, selection records; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\LoopbackTranscriber.cs:142-156, ValidateSelection.)
  2. Native ownership: specify endpoint direction and exact identity matching, construction failure, disconnect, stop, and disposal. WasapiInput distinguishes Render from Capture and releases both endpoint notifications and native capture ownership. Do not substitute a default device after selection fails. (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\WasapiInput.cs:20-74, constructor and MatchesSelection; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\WasapiInput.cs:97-119, Dispose.)
  3. Transport capacity: audit fixed arrays of length three, allowed source counts, byte prefixes, and total pending-byte limits. Those structures encode the present two-source contract. Update resource arithmetic explicitly rather than increasing a limit until tests stop failing. (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:13-18, limits; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:51-56, source-indexed fields; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:104-114, source validation.)
  4. Server symmetry: align SOURCES, canonical source ordering, declared-source validation, per-source rate credits, and queue accounting. Stop must drain source workers and pending finalization, publishing every selected source's final before stopped. (services\transcription\server.py:26-28, source map; services\transcription\server.py:100-112, parse_start; services\transcription\server.py:319-357, Session.receive; services\transcription\server.py:394-498, stop drain.)
  5. UI, tests, privacy, documentation: update selectors, meters, source visibility, export labels, denied-device behavior, and user-facing capture scope. Existing UI branches explicitly on Computer/Microphone/Both; do not let a new value fall into an accidental “Both” default. (src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.xaml.cs:720-760, UpdateAudioControls, SetCaptureMode; tests\PhantomFudge.Audio.Tests\DualSourceTests.cs:17-44, synthetic regression catalogue.)
  6. Question provenance: update TranscriptValidation.Source, structured keys and chooser filters as well as display names. The Mic default must not silently select a new source. All sources is a visibility filter, not authorization to include every row; Use selected still copies only explicit keys. Test new-source partial/final identity and local provenance retention separately from export formatting. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\TranscriptSegment.cs:5-14, TranscriptSegmentKey; src\PhantomFudge.Core\TranscriptSegment.cs:76-80, source validation; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:70-120, filtering/selection.)

Checklist 2: a new recognition backend

Begin at the recognition contract, not the model download. The current hybrid uses independent per-source provisional queues and single-thread workers, plus a separate serial finalizer for retained PCM spans. It does not funnel both stages through one executor. Source decoders produce provisional Recognition or bounded FinalSpan handoffs; finalization produces bounded final text with finite ordered times, and Stop drains pending work before stopped. Decoder faults/timeouts still invalidate readiness; native calls cannot simply be killed safely. Preserve these ordering, ownership and deadline rules when adding a backend. (services\transcription\server.py:115-181, Runtime.cpu and CPU ownership; services\transcription\server.py:361-498, Session.publish, recognize.) The current Runtime.source_cpu/final_cpu and Session.recognize_source/finalize separate source progress from expensive finalization; publication remains serialized.

Specify the backend's answers to five questions:

  • Does accept produce useful revisable partials, completed text, or bounded PCM-span handoffs?
  • Does finish flush every processed sample, and does it permit continuation?
  • Are timestamps cumulative, and how are reset offsets preserved?
  • Can independent source decoders share immutable model weights without sharing recognition history?
  • Are inference and setup strictly separated so recognition cannot trigger an implicit download?

VoskFactory and VoskRecognizer still supply verified local models, independent provisional decoders and the explicit Vosk-only alternative; their absolute-timing/source-isolation tests remain relevant, but do not describe the whole hybrid. (services\transcription\recognizer.py:25-66, verify_model, VoskFactory; services\transcription\recognizer.py:69-110, VoskRecognizer; services\transcription\tests\test_recognizer.py:37-75, RecognizerTests.) The production default is hybrid-whisper / small.en: Vosk supplies streaming provisional text while CPU/int8 Whisper finalizes disjoint retained spans. HybridRecognizer cuts spans at an endpoint, its bounded rotation threshold or Stop; WhisperFinalizer uses explicitly provisioned local files rather than downloading during recognition. (services\transcription\configuration.py:12-34, DEFAULT, load_config; services\transcription\accurate.py:33-71, HybridRecognizer; services\transcription\accurate.py:74-129, WhisperFinalizer, HybridFactory.)

Do not advertise batch throughput as streaming latency. The earlier benchmark/research recommendation for optional question-only Whisper refinement is historical, not the current hybrid runtime configuration. Current Whisper finalization also does not remove Vosk's streaming provisional role or establish a live-latency guarantee. Any later recognition result must respect edit/snapshot ownership: it cannot overwrite user-edited text or mutate an already-frozen question. Backend changes still require protocol, UI, privacy, model-provenance and benchmark review even when their wire shape stays unchanged. (docs\SPEECH-BENCHMARK.md:34-40, historical recommendation; docs\AI-ANSWER-RESEARCH.md:90-99, earlier optional-refinement research; src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionDraft.cs:48-79, edit/refresh; src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionSnapshot.cs:5-23, immutability.)

Checklist 3: a new theme or semantic color role

Theme changes have a narrower code surface but a wider visual evidence surface. ThemePalette.For provides semantic colors; ThemeBrushes.Apply maps those roles into both application resources and standard WPF control resources. Adding a role requires checking each palette and its consumers, not inserting an isolated literal into one control. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\ThemePalette.cs:5-26, ThemePalette.For; src\PhantomFudge.App\ThemeBrushes.cs:9-32, Apply.)

Review text, muted text, headings, selection foreground/background, action text, warning/error, input, hover, and border states. Preserve frozen brushes and dynamic-resource bindings. Also decide whether a new theme participates in the two-theme toggle: NextThemed currently alternates the companions and exits Plain toward DeepSeaFoam. That behavior is tested and should not change accidentally. (src\PhantomFudge.App\ThemeBrushes.cs:35-41, Brush; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.xaml:116-163, dynamic resources; src\PhantomFudge.Core\ThemePalette.cs:28-29, NextThemed; tests\PhantomFudge.Core.Tests\ThemePaletteTests.cs:19-25, toggle test.)

The background slider controls the shared translucent backdrop visible behind notes, transcript and question/answer reading surfaces. Its setter changes the root brush alpha; transparent Q/A panels and editors let that backdrop show through while reading text remains fully opaque. Do not reintroduce an opaque answer background that masks the slider, or “simplify” this into whole-window opacity that fades text. The QuestionPanel, QuestionEditor, QuestionSnapshotText and AnswerText declarations make this composition explicit. Existing contrast tests cover opaque reading/selection pairs, not arbitrary content behind a translucent window. Recheck actual UI, focus/hit regions and capture scenarios without promoting local rendering into meeting compatibility. (src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.xaml.cs:482-505, opacity and ApplyTheme; tests\PhantomFudge.Core.Tests\ThemePaletteTests.cs:31-40, opaque contrast test; docs\QUALIFICATION.md:111-145, transition matrix.)

Include the local question pane in that review: selected rows, editable/read-only draft, provisional/user-edited indicators and read-only snapshot are different visual states. Verify that theme switching preserves their text; an immutable snapshot alone does not prove visual correctness, recipient invisibility or every contrast combination. (src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:198-208, interaction states; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:246-259, provenance display; src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionSnapshot.cs:5-23, immutable snapshot.)

Checklist 4: a provider is a new trust boundary

Answer providers must stay separate from local speech transport. Do not loosen ValidateEndpoint to accommodate cloud inference or a model server: it deliberately accepts only literal loopback addresses and the exact transcription path. A second loopback API is not the same protocol simply because both run locally. (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:82-98, ValidateEndpoint.)

The future Azure checklist—explicit Ask, destination approval, identity, bounds, cancellation, terminal reasons and safe output—still applies. Installed-CLI integration makes those concerns immediate rather than proving them solved. Render text as data, not XAML/HTML, commands or automatically opened links. Offline fake-stream/process checks must precede a real-call receipt. (TODO\31_STREAMING_ANSWER_CLIENT.todo:13-28, provider contract; TODO\34_ANSWER_PRIVACY_RESILIENCE.todo:13-28, failure/privacy gates; docs\AI-ANSWER-PRIVACY.md:132-149, output and logging boundaries.)

The snapshot remains a local provenance contract, not a provider DTO. Repeated Freeze can retain the same question ID/revision, so an answer attempt needs its own identity. Keep mode-specific notices: “nothing sent” is correct for SnapshotOnly, not a guarantee for configured Agency, whose model service may be remote. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionSnapshot.cs:5-23, snapshot data; src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionDraft.cs:90-95, Freeze; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:265-305, snapshot action.)

Review these additional concrete surfaces before extending the new common interface:

  1. Request projection: AnswerRun generates a fresh GUID and normally passes only ExactText; SourceRefs, notes, audio and unselected text stay outside AnswerRequest. The explicitly requested, default-off Clarify first option adds typed instruction/history metadata. Separately, Previous answer may add one displayed completed answer in nullable PreviousAnswer; null preserves the existing direct path. Do not widen these exceptions into generic app context or recursively serialize earlier requests. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerContracts.cs:5-31, request/events/interface; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerRun.cs:15-29, projection.)
  2. Settings versus readiness: Agency mode adds AgencyPath for the supported agency copilot launcher; local installation is not offline inference or authorization to inspect organization data. LocalModel remains the separate Copilot-engine OFFLINE/BYOK route to an explicit literal-loopback /v1 server. Destination validation cannot verify model installation or prevent server-side proxying. No hosted-model fallback is permitted. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerContracts.cs:41-74, settings validation.)
  3. Executable and profile authority: setup resolves Agency without login; a .exe path is not proof of authenticity or isolation. Preserve the pinned profile-only launch and reject ambient hooks, permissions, plugins, MCPs and resumed sessions. The exact generated direct-Q&A agent is a deliberate controlled exception, not permission to import a personal coding agent. Missing existing authentication must not trigger app-owned login/account switching. These controls are not an OS sandbox or organization-data grant. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerContracts.cs:47-52, syntactic validation; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerConfiguration.cs:8-29, profile/settings paths.)
  4. Terminal protocol: TextDelta/Completed retain request IDs and increasing sequence. Completion carries no text and only latches a marker; nonblank text and clean request enumeration end are also required. The persistent engine's pipe must not close after each answer. Test duplicate, late, wrong-request and post-terminal events without turning raw diagnostics into answers. The 32,768-unit cap rejects an overflowing delta whole. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerRun.cs:34-65, Apply, Complete.)
  5. Ownership and retention: one active request, a 120-second deadline and 40-ms render timer remain unchanged. Cancel/Hide/Clear/protection/reload/close must reach the cached provider and await owned cleanup, even during preparation. Keep partials incomplete and Copy deliberate; never retry/resend automatically. Engine/workspace artifacts can survive individual answers until teardown, so app memory bounds are not end-to-end memory-only operation. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerRun.cs:67-81, Cancel, Fail.) Inspect the lifetime owner and provider guide, not just Core state.

Persistent-provider additions to that checklist

Persistence moves ownership outside a single request's await foreach. A new provider must declare whether success releases a request, conversation, process, workspace or all four. Agency acknowledges session/close before Completed, keeps the engine, then prepares another empty session. It never reuses a question conversation and rotates the engine after at most 32 created sessions. Normal startup/reveal intentionally calls WarmUpAsync, preparing one empty session without a model question. The alternative WarmUpTransportAsync prepares only transport and leaves session creation on Ask; it is not the current app readiness policy. The selected-default preparation took 21.183 seconds with zero questions. Keep that readiness cost separate from prepared completion. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AgencyAcpConnection.cs:41-122, reuse/session/prompt/close; tools\AgencyProbe\results\agency-selected-fast-default-preparation.json:2-16, empty-session preparation; tools\AgencyProbe\results\summary-final.json:210-224, cleanup and retention.)

Before prompt submission, verify advertised configuration: controlled agent, exact requested model, reasoning effort and allow_all=off. CLI --agent alone was insufficient in pinned ACP; explicit session/set_config_option installs the intended SYSTEM-role policy. Preserve one user text containing fixed instructions plus JSON userQuestion, not a serialized snapshot. Normal Ask excludes history; only explicit Clarify first requests may include their bounded typed clarification exchanges. Validate Unicode and escape file-reference syntax while retaining the decoded exact question. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AgencyAcpConnection.cs:61-96, agent selection/one prompt; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AgencyAcpConnection.cs:296-319, configuration validation; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AgencyAnswerPrompt.cs:8-111, controlled policy and envelope.)

The receiver rejects tools, permission/client requests and protocol plans instead of waiting. The full-answer prose check excludes code fences and rejects selected missing-input/follow-up phrases; it is a heuristic, not proof of usefulness. Keep semantic/correctness gates alongside timing: A–C preserved slow/generic/clarification failures; D failed eight overflow checks; E passed a surrogate question set; F chose wrong problems; G omitted full-range arithmetic safeguards despite correct title interpretation. H passed the finite exact-text contract on the new selected model. Neither three successful samples nor first text establishes a universal complete-answer guarantee. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AgencyAcpConnection.cs:213-265, rejected requests/plans; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AgencyAcpConnection.cs:330-354, heuristic; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AgencyAnswerPrompt.cs:12-43, answer policy; tools\AgencyProbe\results\summary-final.json:109-180, retained failures and selected result.)

A default-model change also has a display and diagnostics surface. Keep the provider's public DefaultModel/EffectiveModel as the source of truth; the UI ProviderLabel already derives its default from that property, so recompilation updates the label. Preserve explicit overrides, fixed safe model metadata and no fallback. A newly compiled default is not itself a new latency measurement of the app binary. (tools\AgencyProbe\results\summary-final.json:234-260, measurement assembly and public model properties.)

Finally, extend diagnostics without silently extending disclosure. Default events have correlation, duration/process/count/code fields; bodies require explicit content opt-in. Preserve the nonblocking queue and bounded file retention. The diagnostic constructor must suppress real warm-up, and fixtures must not turn session preparation into a cloud question. See diagnostics. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Diagnostics\LocalDiagnostics.cs:9-24, metadata schema; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Diagnostics\LocalDiagnostics.cs:40-111, bounds; src\PhantomFudge.Core\Diagnostics\LocalDiagnostics.cs:145-184, content opt-in.)

Cloud ASR changes audio egress; an enterprise broker changes authentication, routing, hosting, and streaming behavior. Neither is a routine interchangeable implementation detail. Both need separately justified policy and evaluation decisions, and neither makes Docker an ordinary runtime requirement. (TODO\36_OPTIONAL_AZURE_SPEECH.todo:13-25, optional Speech; TODO\37_OPTIONAL_ANSWER_BROKER.todo:13-26, optional broker.)

Checklist 5: a new state field is a lifecycle change

For every proposed field, write down its owner, creation boundary, mutation authority, reset rule, serialization version, memory bound and logging/export policy. Existing display-buffer BeginSession resets final numbering, while AddFinal deduplicates globally within that session. The new structured key therefore separates capture identity from protocol final numbering. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\TranscriptBuffer.cs:23-38, BeginSession; src\PhantomFudge.Core\TranscriptBuffer.cs:48-72, AddFinal; src\PhantomFudge.Core\TranscriptSegment.cs:3-20, TranscriptSegmentKey.)

The implemented local fields provide a concrete lifecycle checklist:

Field or owner Preserve this invariant when extending it
Capture GUID / local utterance ID New capture identity per Start; partial→final retains its local key. Store Clear does not recycle local IDs.
Source epoch Current UI events use local 0; a field's existence is not wire negotiation or commit support.
Selected records Copies survive 256-entry/64,000-character store eviction; reject cross-session selection.
Draft revision / user edit Compose and validate the full 8,192-character candidate before assignment; explicit editing blocks ASR replacement.
Frozen snapshot Copy provenance/text; future draft changes cannot mutate a previously returned snapshot.
Answer request/run New GUID per attempt, exact-text-only request, increasing event sequence and a terminal marker distinct from completed state.
Cached engine / readiness Distinguish transport from empty-session readiness; stop/dispose on owner teardown, not merely at enumeration end.
Prepared session / model One prompt maximum, unique session identity, exact configured role/model and bounded engine rotation.

Sources: (src\PhantomFudge.Core\StructuredTranscriptStore.cs:13-34, capacity/session; src\PhantomFudge.Core\StructuredTranscriptStore.cs:76-109, final identity/Clear); (src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:134-142, epoch-default calls); (src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionDraft.cs:18-79, selection/refresh transaction); (src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionSnapshot.cs:5-23, immutable copy).

The answer fields have their own lifecycle in (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerRun.cs:15-65, constructor, Apply, Complete). They must not reset transcription IDs or turn a new draft revision into a hidden resend.

An empty final is not permission to retain the last guessed partial: it settles that selected record to empty. Blank editing remains possible, but blank Ask rejects. Oversized selection, edit or refresh must leave the prior draft intact; do not “help” by truncating its meaning. Preserve the staged-update pattern when adding fields. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\StructuredTranscriptStore.cs:80-86, empty final; src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionDraft.cs:90-124, Freeze, Compose; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:214-243, edit/paste rejection.)

Wire evolution is especially surgical. The current service requires exact start objects, accepts only Stop after start, and the C# client checks exact response property sets. Even an apparently optional extra JSON field can break compatibility. Preserve v1/v2 behavior and negotiate a new version or capability rather than silently weakening parsers. (services\transcription\server.py:100-112, parse_start; services\transcription\server.py:306-316, Session.receive; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:491-515, RequireTranscriptProperties, RequireProperties.)

Focus is also state, not decoration. PassiveWindow depends on presentation and question editing. The separate question path deliberately focuses typing without stopping audio or enabling Notes editing; global Notes Edit/Present/Hide behavior is not redefined. New answer controls must preserve that distinction while adding their own cancellation lifetime. Check protection readiness, file-busy rejection, return to passive interaction and audio-start cancellation independently. (src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:24-25, PassiveWindow; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:156-208, focus transition.)

This is a recommended engineering workflow, not an executed release pipeline. Qualification must identify the exact packaged candidate and distinguish source tests, UI observations, recipient capture evidence, and owner approval. A successful build cannot fill an untested sharing-product row. (docs\QUALIFICATION.md:3-7, current matrix; docs\QUALIFICATION.md:150-176, result record; TODO\35_ANSWER_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.todo:13-26, candidate acceptance.)

Worked pseudocode: evolving local epochs into negotiated commit

SourceEpoch already exists locally; current v2 ingestion supplies 0. TODO29 requires a producer/consumer agreement for armed start/end boundaries, ordered sample coverage and acknowledged epoch advancement—not merely another field. The following future commit matrix extends existing local guards; its transition functions are illustrative, not implemented APIs. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\TranscriptSegment.cs:17-20, key fields; src\PhantomFudge.App\MainWindow.Questions.cs:134-142, v2 ingestion.)

cases = [
    ("same_session_same_epoch", "accept"),
    ("old_session_same_segment_id", "reject_stale"),
    ("old_epoch_after_commit", "reject_stale"),
    ("duplicate_commit_same_parameters", "replay_ack"),
    ("duplicate_commit_changed_watermark", "reject"),
    ("late_final_after_user_edit", "preserve_user_revision"),
    ("selected_record_evicted", "preserve_local_copy"),
    ("freeze_then_late_final", "preserve_exact_snapshot"),
    ("new_field_sent_to_v2_peer", "reject_protocol"),
]
for scenario, expected in cases:
    state, event = synthetic_fixture(scenario)
    before = snapshot_unrelated_source(state)
    actual = proposed_transition(state, event)
    assert actual == expected
    assert unrelated_source(state) == before
    assert no_request_was_sent_without_explicit_ask(state)

This matrix connects protocol changes to UI/privacy consequences. Existing local guards do not establish a sample-exact live-Mic span from v2 text. Future commit must finalize only Mic, preserve Computer capture and use processed—not merely received—sample coverage. Tests should use generated data and injected capture, not silently open hardware. (tests\PhantomFudge.Core.Tests\SourceTranscriptTests.cs:5-56, source isolation tests; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\LoopbackTranscriber.cs:25-28, synthetic capture seam; TODO\29_QUESTION_COMMIT_LATENCY.todo:13-28, proposed commit requirements.)

Tradeoffs and the final change-surface review

Before calling a surgical change complete, review six surfaces even when some require no edit:

Surface Question to answer in the change record
UI Did focus, protection lifecycle, source visibility, or status meaning change?
Protocol Can an older peer reject, misinterpret, or accept an unsupported message?
Tests Which existing invariant survives, and which new failure ordering is exercised?
Privacy Did captured, transmitted, retained, logged, or exported data expand?
Resources Are per-source limits, total limits, deadlines, and cleanup still bounded?
Documentation Are implemented behavior, proposed behavior, and qualification gaps still distinguishable?

This checklist synthesizes the existing strict transport, resource controls, and qualification record rather than introducing a new runtime framework. “No change required” is useful only when accompanied by the reason: a palette-only edit may leave framing unchanged, while a provider edit necessarily revisits egress and credential handling. (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:13-18, limits; src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:512-515, strict properties; docs\QUALIFICATION.md:150-176, evidence record; docs\AI-ANSWER-PRIVACY.md:132-151, provider safeguards.)

Prefer a smaller supported contract over a permissive parser or automatic fallback that conceals unsupported behavior. Preserve failed and untested outcomes in the handoff: a new backend passing synthetic tests does not qualify a new window surface, a real microphone, or a cloud data policy. (docs\QUALIFICATION.md:24-26, outcome vocabulary; TODO\35_ANSWER_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.todo:23-26, acceptance boundaries.)

  1. Find every fixed two-source assumption in the checklist. Explain why changing only the enum can compile in one layer while violating another layer's runtime schema. (src\PhantomFudge.App\Audio\TranscriptionSocket.cs:51-56, arrays; services\transcription\server.py:100-112, parse_start.)
  2. Propose a warning color with acceptable opaque contrast, then explain why translucent-background readability still needs separate observation. (tests\PhantomFudge.Core.Tests\ThemePaletteTests.cs:31-73, contrast calculation; docs\PRODUCT.md:121-128, translucency limits.)
  3. Draft a provider change receipt that records capability and privacy differences without including a real question, token, or account secret. (docs\AI-ANSWER-EVALUATION.md:140-149, receipt requirements.)
  4. Select a partial, freeze it, edit the draft, then deliver an empty final and evict the original store row. Explain each object's expected text and why SourceRefs must not become the Azure request body. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionDraft.cs:48-95, edit/refresh/Freeze; src\PhantomFudge.Core\QuestionSnapshot.cs:5-23, local immutable provenance.)
  5. On paper, apply TextDelta(1), Completed(2), then TextDelta(3) to one run; contrast that with request enumeration ending before Completed. Explain why neither is complete, why ACP process EOF is a different failure, and why none permits provider fallback. (src\PhantomFudge.Core\Answers\AnswerRun.cs:34-65, event/terminal guards.)
